info.title: OnDemand Spatial Satellites (CelesTrak)
info.description: Live satellite situational awareness from CelesTrak general-perturbation element sets, propagated server-side with SGP4: which satellites are over a place right now (with altitude, speed, ground distance and observer look angles) and when a given satellite — the ISS, Tiangong, a GPS/GLONASS/Galileo vehicle, a geostationary bird or a Starlink — next rises, culminates and sets for an observer. Backed by the same cached, fallback-protected CelesTrak proxy the OnDemand Spatial satellites layer uses; answers carry a provider status (live / stale / degraded / unavailable) and element-set provenance.

conversationStarters: Which satellites are over Austin, Texas right now within 1000 km?
When does the ISS next pass over London above 10° elevation?
List the GPS satellites currently above the horizon for 48.85, 2.35.
Show the next Tiangong (CSS) passes over Tokyo in the coming 48 hours.
Are any geostationary satellites within 2000 km of the sub-satellite point over Nairobi?
x-ondemand-spatial.auth: none — same-origin proxy; upstream credentials stay server-side

get.summary: Satellites currently over a scene (SGP4 from CelesTrak TLEs)
get.description: Propagates every satellite of the requested CelesTrak groups to the current time with SGP4 and returns those whose sub-satellite point lies within radiusKm of the scene point and whose elevation for an observer at that point is at least minElevationDeg. Results are sorted nearest-first and capped by limit; each row carries the sub-satellite latitude/longitude, altitude, speed, ground distance and the observer look angles (elevation, azimuth, slant range). Groups: stations (ISS, Tiangong, crewed/cargo vehicles), visual (brightest objects), gps-ops, glo-ops, galileo (navigation constellations), geo (geostationary belt) and starlink (large; opt-in). Use minElevationDeg ≥ 0 to keep only satellites above the local horizon.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Scene / observer latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84).

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Scene / observer longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84).

parameters.name: radiusKm
parameters.description: Maximum ground distance (km) from the scene point to a satellite sub-satellite point. Default 1500.

parameters.name: groups
parameters.description: Comma-separated CelesTrak groups to search: stations, visual, gps-ops, glo-ops, galileo, geo, starlink. Default stations,visual,gps-ops,glo-ops,galileo,geo.

parameters.name: minElevationDeg
parameters.description: Minimum elevation (degrees above the horizon) for an observer at the scene point. Default -90 (no elevation filter); use 0 for "above the horizon", 10 for comfortably visible.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of satellites returned (nearest first). Default 50.

502.description: Upstream failure with a structured reason

503.description: Provider unavailable (missing key / no data) with a structured reason

get.summary: Upcoming passes of one satellite over an observer
get.description: Predicts the rise, culmination and set times of one satellite (identified by NORAD catalogue id or a case-insensitive name substring such as "ISS" or "TIANGONG") for an observer at lat/lon over the next `hours`, using SGP4 on the newest CelesTrak element set. The `group` is searched first, then every other CelesTrak group (starlink last). Each pass reports UTC rise/max/set times, the maximum elevation, duration and rise/set azimuths; a pass already under way at the window start is flagged inProgress. Exactly one of noradId or name must be supplied. A satellite that is not in any group answers 404 not_found.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Scene / observer latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84).

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Scene / observer longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84).

parameters.name: noradId
parameters.description: NORAD catalogue number of the satellite (e.g. 25544 for the ISS). Supply either noradId or name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive satellite name substring (e.g. "ISS", "CSS (TIANHE)", "HST"). An exact name match wins over a substring match. Supply either noradId or name.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: CelesTrak group to search first (default stations); the other groups are searched when the satellite is not found there.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Prediction window length in hours from now. Default 24.

parameters.name: minElevationDeg
parameters.description: Elevation threshold (degrees) that defines a pass. Default 10.

parameters.name: stepSec
parameters.description: Coarse propagation step in seconds (rise/set are refined by bisection). Default 30.
